# CONVENTIONS
Schema edition 2026-09-29 · kit edition 2026-09-29 · created 2026-09-29
Every convention, blueprint correction, examiner rule and schema change is dated here (P§21).

## 2026-09-29 · Batch 0
- **Auto-vault.** Artifact "PHY-042 VAULT" = https://claude.ai/artifact/B7cPAEtFTDXQKCxkXD8PZY (capabilities db + assets). Round-trip test PASS: db-export -> write_db (20 writes) -> read_db (meta 1 + vault 19) -> db-import into scratch -> 19/19 files byte-identical. vault_url stored in STATE.
- **Kit location.** The project copy is named `pyqkit_py.txt`; the CI§3 pattern `pyqkit*.py*` does not match it. Boot also looks for `pyqkit_py.txt` (logged in Q-QUEUE as a CI conflict).
- **Syllabus verified (PHY-05 vs Physics_SecP2_2026-27.pdf).** All 108 IN topics map to the Class XII theory text (pp. 13-16); every limitation note matches the printed wording; the 21 VERIFY-DEL and 1 DELETED topics are absent from the syllabus text. VERIFY-DEL is kept (the NCERT rationalised list is not in the project). Paraphrase noted, not an error: T-04-02 says "field on the axis of a circular loop"; the syllabus says "application to current carrying circular loop".
- **Unit marks (image p12):** I+II 16 · III+IV 17 · V+VI 18 · VII+VIII 12 · IX 7 · total 70. The Unit IX cell PRINTS 7 and its chapter line reads "Chapter-14". PHY-04 §1's "Chapter 7-14" and "blank Unit IX cell" are text-layer damage (the 7 slides out of its cell), not errors in the document. VERIFIED on image.
- **Thinking-level design (image p23):** Remember+Understand 27 (38 %) · Apply 22 (32 %) · Analyse+Evaluate+Create 21 (30 %); theory 70 + practical 30. The p23 note points to the "Sample Question Paper of class XII for the year 2026-27".
- **Syllabus intro** reads "Class XI-XII (2025-26)" at the top of p1 and "Class XI-XII (2026-27)" at its foot (text layer; p1 image not viewed).
- **Sample paper in the project is the 2025-26 SQP** (p1 image: "CLASS - XII (2025 - 26)"; footer: the 2024-25 scheme "will continue in the current session i.e. 2025-26"). It is the sample paper for the 2026 exam: paper_id SQP2526-042, exam SQP, year 2026. It is mined at Batch 0 and belongs to the 2026 year for the Definition of Done. PHY-04 §2's SQP 2026-27 details (VI alternative inside Q9; text damage 168O, "B and B", 300 for 30 deg) are absent from this file, so PHY-04 §2 describes a different document (the official 2026-27 SQP, not in the project).
- **SQP 2025-26 scoring lines.** No SQP scheme is in the project. Its steps are written in the Y2026 scheme pass: TRANSFERRED:<award_id> from printed 2026 board-scheme steps of the same archetype, otherwise INFERRED (labelled). Never mixed with PRINTED.
- **2027 blueprint.** Until an SQP 2026-27 BLUEPRINTS row exists, plan-mock uses the kit default P33 (choice at 20, 21, 27, 31-33), which is also what SQP 2025-26 prints (see its BLUEPRINTS row).
- **W-1 scheme-year check.** The rotating schemes XII-2-042-*.pdf are 2026 board schemes (55/1/1 image: "MARKING SCHEME: PHYSICS (042) Session: 2025-26 Code: 55/1/1"). They match the next year to mine (2026). Each file's identity is confirmed on its own image at Y2026 S1.
- **FILES status changes** go through ERRATA rows (Layer 1 is append-only); ids ER-B<nn>-<nnn>.
- **Part rows.** Printed sub-part labels ((I), (II), (A), (B), (a), (i) ...) become separate rows with the label as printed in `part`. Unlabelled linked demands ("... Hence define ...") stay one row unless they test different skeletons (then -d1/-d2). The kit counts one event per (paper, question, side, code), so parts sharing a code are never double-counted. The suffix -VI is reserved for visually-impaired alternatives.
- **FORMULAE role `asked`** holds the relation a printed demand requires (read from the demand on the page image, not from a scheme); `given` holds formulas printed in the stem.
- **VI alternatives in SQP 2025-26** sit inside Q5, Q6, Q7, Q18 and Q20(II) (so far); none of them is counted in marks.
- **Classification rule (P§10.2 applied, 2026-09-29).** A row takes an existing code only when its demand is that archetype's core demand and the archetype's scoring skeleton earns full marks on it with no new idea; a narrower or different demand (e.g. "write the expression" against "derive it") gets its own code in the same family. MCQ and A-R items get their own "(MCQ)" / "(A-R)" codes (P§10.3.5), including MCQ sub-parts of case studies. Labelled parts that share one skeleton share one code (one event).
- **VI alternatives** are classified only when an existing code fits cleanly; the rest stay unclassified. VI rows never enter statistics or the Definition of Done (kit rule), so this loses nothing.
- **Skeletons of codes issued from SQP 2025-26** come from the printed demand (no scheme in the project) and are refined from printed scheme lines when a scheme exercises the same code.

## 2026-09-29 (UTC) · Batch 1
- **2026 series (p1 images).** 55/1 QPSR1 · 55/2 R2SQP · 55/3 PQS3R (+ 55(B), set 5) · 55/4 RP4QS · 55/5 R5QPS · compartment 55/7 S7PQR (+ 55(B)/7, set 5).
- **Letter codes.** The VI papers print "55(B)" and "55(B)/7"; their scheme prints "Code: 55/ B". Written paper_code 55/B and 55/B/7, paper_id 2026-55B and 2026C-55B7, so paper and scheme share one code in COVERAGE.
- **Compartment.** Series 55/7 is recorded exam COMPT, tag 2026C, from ZIP identity (2,364,538 bytes = the official 2026-COMPTT Physics ZIP size in PHY-04 s4; entries dated 2026-07-29) and its separate series. The papers print no exam type.
- **Year evidence, 2026 papers.** No 2026 paper prints a year. Evidence: the same-code scheme printing "Session 2025-26" (image), the PDF creation year, and the official ZIP size; the content match with the scheme is confirmed per paper at S5.
- **Scheme bundles are image-only scans.** Text layer = a contents page on p1 and "HOME" link words elsewhere, so the dual-read is impossible: every scoring line is read from the 924-px JPEG, enlarged; a line still uncertain -> UNREADABLE LOWRES + one optional single-page request. Layout (55/1/1): p1 contents, p2-p3 the 18 examiner instructions + an OSM note on choice questions, p4 onward value points; 55/4/1 starts its value points on p3.
- **Origins.** Set 1 of each series is the S3 origin (all sets are clean originals); siblings and the two VI papers are S4 work of their series.
- **Bilingual originals.** Hindi and English pages alternate, and the kit's page table marks the Hindi pages "en" (their text layer is not Unicode), so English pages are picked per paper at S3 from the page text (55/1/1: odd pages 3-31).
- **Choice inside a case sub-part (2026 boards).** Q29 and Q30 carry an OR alternative inside one sub-part, printed after OR without its own label. Rows: the untouched sub-parts keep side blank (`-Q29-I`); the alternatives take sides A and B at question level with the sub-part label as printed context (`-Q29A-III`, `-Q29B-III`), one choice_pair_id `OR-<paper>-Q29`, and `extra` choice_in_part=III. check-paper counts the question once. BLUEPRINTS choice_rule lists such questions under D (e.g. `D:29,30`).
- **Sides printed as (a) OR (b).** A single-part alternative labelled (a)/(b) (e.g. 55/1/1 Q18) is written as sides A/B with no part; where each side has its own (a), (b) parts, those are the parts (`-Q22A-a`).
- **Printed sub-labels (i), (ii) inside a part** become their own rows (`-Q22A-b-i`), as the Batch 0 part-row rule says.
- **A shared case figure** gets one full FIGURES description on the first dependent row and short pointer rows on the other dependent rows, so every has_figure row has its figure.
- **Documents are opened by file_id**, not paper_id, while Q-008 is open.
- **Kit edition 2026-09-30 (B01).** Two tested fixes, shipped in tools/: (1) check-paper counts side-blank rows as common to both alternatives when a question also has sides A/B, so printed sub-part marks of a case with a choice inside one sub-part (55/2/1 Q29, Q30: 1 mark each) add up to the question total; (2) a paper_id shared by a paper and its scheme resolves to the question paper, and an exact file_id always wins (Q-008). Tests: 2026-5521, 2026-5511 and SQP2526-042 PASS; validate 16/16; a planted sub-part overflow is still caught. Previous edition kept as a local backup only.
- **Reading time** (all 20 papers): the cover note "(V) 15 minute time has been allotted to read this question paper" was checked on the 55/1/1 cover image; the other 19 covers carry the same note in their text layer.
- **S4 method (B01).** Sibling questions are matched to the origin by text similarity, then every sibling page is read on its image. A question with identical text and numbers becomes a shuffle row (a copy of the origin row with the sibling's own id, q_no, source_page, choice and case ids, rel = shuffle, rel_to = origin row); its printed figures and formulae are copied with the sibling's pages. A question that differs in any way is extracted fully as rel = origin, with a note naming the origin question it resembles. The ARSET goes on the sibling's own first assertion-reason row.

## 2026-10-01 (UTC) · Batch 2 · Claude Code route
- **Route.** Mining moved to Claude Code cloud sessions over three GitHub repositories found by content: instructions (read only), project (vault file and the year's schemes; the only repository committed to), papers (question-paper ZIPs; read only). The chat project audits read only while Claude Code mines; its findings arrive as `Fix:` lines (one writer at a time).
- **Checkpoint.** `phy_gate.py` merges part files, writes the status erratum and the PROGRESS line with counts computed from the tables, validates, packs into `outputs/vault/` of the project repository, commits and pushes after every paper. This replaces the auto-vault database and her manual vault swap. `STATE.json` gains the key `cc_session` (additive).
- **Double-read.** From Batch 2, every paper's marks, numbers, options and figure values are read twice: by an extractor and by a blind checker who sees only the row skeleton. The gate compares the two readings; every mismatch is settled from a 300-400 dpi crop and logged (`outputs/logs/GATE-LOG-B02.md`, `outputs/logs/doublecheck/`).
- **Originals.** Files the chat saw as 924-px bundles now come from GitHub as original PDFs with their own FILES rows; each takes its twin's identity through ERRATA (S1b). Scoring lines are read from the originals.
- **Kit edition 2026-09-30b** (made and tested in the chat on 2026-09-30, first used at Batch 2): a row may name its series in `extra` as `series=55/3`; V07 and `similar` use it. The letter-code visually-impaired papers carry it on every row: 2026-55B `series=55/3; vi_paper=y`, 2026C-55B7 `series=55/7; vi_paper=y`, so their unchanged questions are shuffles of their own series and are not counted twice. Tests: validate 16/16 on the Batch 1 vault; a 55B shuffle of a 2026-5531 row passes V07 only with the key; a 55B7 row with `series=55/7` pointing at a 55/3 row fails.
- **S1b result (B02).** 17 originals took their bundle twins' identity (16 2026 schemes and the syllabus; ER-B02-001..ER-B02-071), each confirmed on its own page images: p1 (scheme contents page with "PHYSICS (042) Code: ...", or the 55/4/1 instructions page) and, for the schemes, the first value-point header "MARKING SCHEME: PHYSICS (042) Session: 2025-26 Code: ...". Two new files are not twins: Physics-MS.pdf is the marking scheme of SQP 2025-26 (SQP-MS, SQP2526-042; ER-B02-072..ER-B02-076; Q-012); Physics-SQP (1).pdf is the 2024-25 sample paper (SQP2425-042, stays NEW for its year; ER-B02-077..ER-B02-078).
- **Syllabus p1 (correction to the Batch 0 line "Syllabus intro reads ...").** The original's p1 image prints only "Class XI-XII (2026-27)"; the "(2025-26)" read at the top of p1 in Batch 0 is a hidden object in the text layer, which the image does not show. PHY-04 §1's "intro still says 2025-26" is therefore text-layer damage too (Q-002).
- **Scheme repository (B02 layout).** The 2026 scheme PDFs sit in a repository that holds neither a vault file nor a ZIP, so `phy_code_env.py` gives it no role and links none of its files; the vault file sits in the instructions repository, which therefore also serves as the project repository (`outputs/` and the pushes go there). At B02 the 16 scheme PDFs were linked into /mnt/project by hand (links only, no repository changed) before inventory, which therefore recorded them where=project. Repeat the links at boot until the layout or the setup changes (Q-011).
- **Opening a document by file_id on this route:** `pyqkit pages` and `render` need `--vault /home/claude/vault` (the kit's default vault is empty); R§3's commands omit it (Q-011).
- **A shuffle whose origin row misreads the shared figure (B02).** The row stays rel = shuffle (the page images are identical); its own FIGURES and FORMULAE rows describe what the page shows and its note names the origin rows that disagree; the origin rows change only through ERRATA with crop evidence (a Fix), never by copying the error forward (2026-5532-Q19A; Q-013).

## S5 scheme pass (B02, first scheme 55/1/1)
- **Examiner instructions, 2026 board schemes (55/1/1 pp2-3, register R14):** marks strictly by the value points, but competency-based answers and correct answers from other expressions or newer knowledge get due marks (4, 5); an error is penalised once, never for its cumulative effect (10); full scale 0-70 used (11); a candidate who attempts both alternatives is marked on both and the higher counts (17); an unattempted alternative is marked NA (18); OSM marking, part marks on the right, unparted questions in the left margin (8, 9). No instruction on half marks or units: halves appear only in the value points. Later sets note only differences.
- **Key rows:** an MCQ or assertion-reason answer is one `key` row whose step_text is the printed letter only, e.g. `(C)`, marks 1; the option text it names is already on the paper row. An OR alternative key with no mark printed beside it takes the sub-part's 1.
- **Combined mark cells** ("½ + ½", "½ + ½ + ½" beside one line that lists several items) are one STEP-AWARDS row per printed half, the cell's text kept in each step_text; the blind checker lists them the same way.
- **Unmarked routes:** "Alternatively" methods and "award full marks for any other ..." notes carrying no marks of their own go into `alt_accepted` of the line they replace; they are not scoring lines. `mandatory = y` only where the scheme says a line is compulsory.
- **Scheme symbols** that differ from the paper's (55/1/1 Q24 uses L for the plate separation) are kept as printed in step_text; the mapping note in notes/Y2026.md says what they stand for.
- **A half mark printed between two parts' lines** goes where the scheme's own description box (the per-question split printed at the top of each answer) puts it (55/1/2 Q27: box (b) 1, (c) ½ + 1).
- **Split box against printed line marks:** the box decides only a half mark printed between two parts' lines. A mark printed beside a line belongs to that line's part even when the box says otherwise; the conflict is written in the step_text of the first line of each part and queued (55/4/3 Q28, Q-014).

## 2026-10-02 (UTC) · Batch 3
- **Work order (her decision, 2026-10-02).** Printed documents first, newest year to oldest: 2025, then 2024, 2023, 2022 (Term 2 and Term 1). For each year: S1 intake (PHY-08 Y§2), S2a constants (Y§3), S3 origins and S4 siblings (Y§4), then S5 for every scheme of that year that is in a schemes repository (Y§5); then the next year whose papers are present, without waiting for her. Deferred to the closing sweep after 2022's printed documents: S5 lines for papers without a scheme (TRANSFERRED/INFERRED, they need S6 codes), S6 classification, S7 derive and workbook, S8 year-close, and 2026's open items (Q-010, FILES statuses, the misses of the 53-code prediction). The gate marks those lines DEFERRED; they are skipped when looking for the next line. When a year's papers are done and its schemes are not in a schemes repository, she is told once which to upload and the next year's papers start; the open S5 lines are done when the schemes appear. A scheme is only ever applied to its own paper_id (W-1). 2026's four open lines were deferred at B03 (`--defer-year 2026`). This overrides CI§5's "a later year never starts until the current year closes" (Q-017).
- **Gate edition 2026-10-02.** `phy_gate.py check` (and so skeleton, verify and commit) refuses a row with a blank `rel` and a row that fills `options` when q_type is neither MCQ nor AR. New checkpoint options: `--plan-year <year>` writes a year's PROGRESS lines from FILES after its S1 identity commit (refused while an identity is incomplete); `--defer-year <year>` marks every open line of that year DEFERRED. Every commit and checkpoint rewrites the dashboard `outputs/README.md` (status, every paper's counts, links to reports, logs and the newest vault) and prints its link.
- **Setup edition 2026-10-02b.** `phy_code_env.py` collects vault files from the working trees and from every branch of every repository, restores the newest and carries that branch forward into this session's branch (B03: PHY-VAULT-B02-20261002-0436-5049r.json from claude/beautiful-pascal-k4durg; three stale copies named). It accepts several schemes repositories and several papers repositories: a repository holding only PDFs (schemes, or question papers kept as loose PDFs) gets the role schemes and is linked into /mnt/project; a repository holding a ZIP gets the role papers and is linked into /mnt/user-data/uploads with its loose PDFs. Tool and instruction files a browser saved as `name (1).py` are linked under their plain names, the newest copy wins and a warning names the extra copies. B03 layout: instructions = project (pyq-physics-minning-instructions-updated); papers PHY-PHYSICS-2025 (ZIP + loose PDFs); schemes PHY-PHYSICS-2025-2- (loose 2025 question papers 55/5, 55/6, 55/7), PHY-PHYSICS-2025-2-MS and PHY-PHYSICS-2025-marking-scheme (2025 schemes). Inventory therefore records the 55/5-55/7 papers with where=project; where says only how a file arrived, never its kind (kind and identity come from page 1 at S1).
- **SQP 2026-27 constants (p1 image, 300 dpi crop).** Nine printed: the eight of SQP 2025-26 with the same values, plus "radius of nucleus ≈10^-15 m", a constant no earlier paper prints; written `R_nucleus` = `~1e-15 m` (`~` for the printed ≈). Script check against standard values: every value within its printed rounding (m_p 1.7e-27 kg is 1.6 % above 1.6726e-27, as SQP 2025-26 prints it; R_nucleus is an order of magnitude, R_0 = 1.2e-15 m). The board papers' k_B, m_n and 1/(4*pi*eps0) are not printed on it.
- **2027 blueprint (B03; supersedes the Batch 0 line "2027 blueprint. Until an SQP 2026-27 BLUEPRINTS row exists ...").** The SQP 2026-27 BLUEPRINTS row (SQP2627-042, page 1) is the 2027 blueprint: P33, sections A:1-16:1;B:17-21:2;C:22-28:3;D:29-30:4;E:31-33:5, choice_rule B:20,21;C:27;E:31,32,33, calculators n, constants listed, no reading time printed. It is identical to SQP 2025-26's row and to the kit default, and every page prints "no change in the Question Paper Design and Assessment Pattern for Academic Session 2026-27". plan-mock reads it from this row. One VI alternative only (inside Q9).
- **SQP 2026-27 rows (B03)** follow the SQP 2025-26 conventions: VI alternative as `-VI` (vi_alt = y); printed splits (2+1, 2+2+1, 3+2) mapped to the labelled parts in order with `printed_split` in extra; a marks cell merged across both sides of an OR (Q20, Q27, Q32) gives marks_part only where the split is printed beside the part (Q32(B) blank; CI s2.6); case totals without a printed total from the instructions page (`marks_from`).
- **A printed answer with no mark beside it (B03, SQP 2026-27 scheme).** When a scheme prints an answer for a part but no mark beside it (so the part's lines total less than the paper's marks), the answer is kept as one STEP-AWARDS line with marks 0 and the conflict in its step_text ("printed with no mark of its own ..."); no mark is ever moved or invented (CI s2.6), and the conflict is queued. Used for SQP2627-042-Q21A-II, -Q22-I, -Q25-II, -Q33B-II-d1 (Q-021). Unmarked alternative routes still go to alt_accepted (CONVENTIONS S5 B02).
- **SQP 2026-27 scheme (FL-7aec844a3c) layout.** No examiner-instructions page; answers numbered as the paper (Q22 prints no I/II labels; its lines are mapped by content; Q33(B)'s "I" covers the paper's (I) and the resonant-frequency expression, its "II" the paper's unlabelled third demand). Text layer present: digits dual-read (known damage: 10^8 as "108", 30 deg as "300").
- **Y2025 series (p1 images, B03).** Main: 55/1 XYW1Z (sets 1-3; cover label "Code No."; image-only scans, 24 pages), 55/2 YXZW2 (sets 1-3; "Code No."; image-only scans, 24 pages), 55/4 X4YZW (sets 1-3; 31 pages) + 55(B) (series X4YZW, set 5: the visually-impaired paper of series 55/4; image-only scan, 24 pages), 55/5 YWX5Z/5 (27 pages), 55/6 6ZXWY/6 (31 pages), 55/7 WX7ZY/7 (31 pages); no 55/3 file was received. Compartment: 55/S WXYZ/S (sets 1-3, 27 pages) + 55(B)/S (set 5, VI), exam COMPT, paper_ids 2025C-55S1..3 and 2025C-55BS, from the ZIP identity (Physics.zip, 1993308 bytes = the 1.90 MB official 2025-COMPTT Physics ZIP of PHY-04 s4; entries dated 2025-07-15) and the separate series; the papers print no exam type. Letter codes: 55(B) -> paper_code 55/B, 2025-55B; 55(B)/S -> 55/B/S, 2025C-55BS.
- **Y2025 schemes (W-1).** Seven files, each printing "Marking Scheme Strictly Confidential (For Internal and Restricted use only) Senior School Certificate Examination, 2025" on the header of every set section: one file per series holding sets 1-3 in three sections, each with its own 18 general instructions (55/1 pp1-19/20-37/38-55; 55/2 pp1-19/20-39/40-57; 55/4 pp1-20/21-42/43-62; 55/5 pp1-16/17-32/33-48; 55/6 pp1-18/19-35/36-52; 55/7 pp1-17/18-33/34-50), and 55/B (14 pages). FILES carry sets_covered 1,2,3 and paper_id of set 1; each set's S5 unit uses its own paper_id and its section's pages. They have text layers (dual-read possible, unlike 2026's scans). Every scheme matches the 2025 exams. No scheme for the compartment series 55/S or 55(B)/S.
- **Y2025 year evidence.** No 2025 paper prints a year; main papers take it from the same-code scheme's examination line ("Senior School Certificate Examination, 2025", image), compartment papers from the ZIP identity; PDF metadata 2025 on all.
- **Y2025 instructions pages (S2a, B03; p3 images, constants from 300 dpi crops).** All 23 papers print the same eleven constants as 2026 with the same values (c, h, e, mu0, eps0, 1/(4*pi*eps0), m_e, m_n, m_p, Avogadro's number, Boltzmann constant), on p3 (English page; p2 is the Hindi page of the scans); 55(B)/S splits them, c to 1/(4*pi*eps0) on p3 and m_e to k_B on p5 (p4 is Hindi). Script check: every value within its printed rounding of the standard value. Wording variants: Section A is "Multiple Choice (MCQ) type questions" (55/1), "Multiple Choice type questions" (55/2, 55/4-55/7, 55/S, 55(B)/S), "Multiple Choice (MCQ), Assertion and Reasoning type questions" (55(B)); (viii) "an internal choice has been provided in few questions in all the Sections except Section A"; (ix) "a separate question paper for Visually Impaired candidates"; "Boltzman's constant" (sic, 55/2 sets). The 15-minute reading note (cover note V) is in the text layer of every text paper; the scans' covers are read with their S3/S4 pass.
- **Nuclide notation (B03 note).** Two written forms are in the vault: mass number over atomic number, '235/92 U', '2/1 H', '12/6 C', '1/0 n' (most rows, 2025 included), and 'C-12 (Z = 6)' (a 2026 list of nuclides; SQP2627-042-Q24 'O-16 (Z = 8)'). Both carry the printed A and Z; new rows use the first form unless the page lists nuclides by name.
- **Her decision 2026-10-03: no blind double-read from 2025-5513 on.** She stopped the second (blind checker) reading to save usage: each paper and scheme gets one thorough reading by the extractor, who re-reads every number, mark, option and direction against its own crop before the gate check. Commits go through the gate with `--unverified "her decision 2026-10-03: single thorough reading, no blind checker"`, so each such unit is queued for a possible later blind check (the gate's own Q-QUEUE item). Papers saved before this date (SQP2627-042, 2025-5511 ... 2025-5571, 2025C-55S1, 2025-5512) kept the full double-read.
- **Examiner instructions, 2025 board schemes (S5, B03; 55/1/1 pp1-2; 55/1/2 and 55/1/3 word for word the same apart from code and page count).** Same as 2026: due credit for answers based on latest knowledge, innovative or competency-based answers (3) and for the candidate's own correct expression (4); an error is penalised once (10); full scale 0-70 (11); no rule on half marks or units. Different from 2026: marking by hand on the answer book, part marks on the right and the total encircled in the left margin (7, 8), with no on-screen-marking wording; in place of 2026's "both alternatives marked, the higher counts" and "an unattempted alternative is NA" (2026 rules 17, 18), rule 9 keeps the higher-scoring answer to an extra question and scores out the other as "Extra Question". New in 2025: 8-hour days with 20-25 answer books a day (12), an error checklist (13), a totally incorrect answer marked X and given zero (14), photocopies of answer books on payment (18). Alternatives printed with their own halves go to alt_accepted as "Alternatively (printed ...): ...", as 2026 did, so a part's lines still add up to its marks.

# PROGRESS — Physics (042) mining
Resume rule: continue from the first unticked line. A ticked item is never redone.

## Done
- Vault created (2026-09-29).
- [x] B0 boot: kit found (project copy `pyqkit_py.txt`), vault initialised, seeded (130 topics, 141 DRAFT archetypes), inventory (38 documents, batch 0)
- [x] B0 syllabus verified against the official 2026-27 syllabus (topics, limitations, unit marks, design table)
- [x] B0 auto-vault published and round-trip tested: PASS

## Next (Claude's work, in order)
- [x] B0 S2 blueprint SQP2526-042 (P33 confirmed; choice B:20,21 C:27 E:31-33)
- [x] B0 S3 SQP2526-042 ledger (check-paper PASS 33/33, 70/70)
- [x] B0 S6 classify SQP2526-042 (71 rows; 19 seeds promoted, 34 codes issued; 7 VI rows left unclassified by policy)
- [x] B0 S7 derive (registers, 14 chapter cards, index; workbook comes with the 2026 close)
- [x] B0 S8 validate + pack + auto-vault

PH-01-001,FAM-01-06 Charge properties,01,T-01-01,DEF,State quantisation and conservation of charge,"Asks you to say that charge comes only in whole-number multiples of e and that total charge never changes, with an example.",Statement q = ne; meaning; conservation statement; example,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-002,FAM-01-01 Coulomb's law and superposition,01,T-01-03,NUM,Find the net Coulomb force on one charge from several charges,Asks you to find each push or pull on one charge separately and add them as arrows to get the total force.,"forces on one charge from the others, their nature and the angle between them (1/2); parallelogram law F_net = sqrt(F_1^2 + F_2^2 + 2*F_1*F_2*cos(theta)) (1/2); substitute F_1 = F_2 = F, theta = 60 deg (1/2); F_net = sqrt(3)*(1/(4*pi*eps0))*(q^2/a^2) (1/2)",Taking the wrong angle between the two repulsive forces (2026 55/B Q31(b)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-55B-Q31A-b,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-55B-Q31A-b; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-01-003,FAM-01-01 Coulomb's law and superposition,01,T-01-03,NUM,Find where a third charge feels zero net force,Asks you to find the point near two charges where their forces on a third charge cancel.,Equate magnitudes; solve for distance; check side; answer with unit,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-004,FAM-01-02 Electric field and field lines,01,T-01-05,NUM,Find the electric field at a point due to several charges,Asks you to find the field from each charge at a point and add them as arrows.,E = (1/(4*pi*eps0))*q/r^2 for each charge (1/2); substitute for each charge (1/2); vector sum of the fields with their directions (1/2); direction of the net field stated (1/2),Leaving out the direction of the net field loses its half mark (2026 55/5/3 Q25(b)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5553-Q25-b,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5553-Q25-b; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-01-005,FAM-01-02 Electric field and field lines,01,T-01-06,CON,State properties of field lines and why they never cross,Asks you to list how electric field lines behave and explain why two of them can never intersect.,Properties list; reason: field has one direction at a point,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-006,FAM-01-02 Electric field and field lines,01,T-01-06,GRF,Sketch field lines for given charge arrangements,Asks you to draw the field-line pattern around given charges with correct directions and spacing.,"Start on +, end on -; arrows; density shows strength; symmetry",,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-007,FAM-01-03 Electric dipole,01,T-01-07,DRV,Derive the field of a dipole on its axial line,"Asks you to show step by step how the field on the dipole's axis depends on distance, ending at 2kp/r^3 far away.",Diagram; fields of +q and -q; subtract; simplify; far-field limit; direction,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-008,FAM-01-03 Electric dipole,01,T-01-07,DRV,Derive the field of a dipole on its equatorial line,"Asks you to show step by step how the field on a dipole's equatorial line works out, and how it simplifies far away, pointing opposite to the dipole moment.","figure: dipole, point P on the equatorial plane at r, both fields (1/2); E_+q = E_-q = (1/(4*pi*eps0))*q/(r^2 + a^2) (1/2); normal components cancel, components along the axis add: vec(E) = -(E_+q + E_-q)*cos(theta) p^ (1); vec(E) = -(1/(4*pi*eps0))*2qa/(r^2 + a^2)^(3/2) p^ (1/2); r >> a: vec(E) = -2qa/(4*pi*eps0*r^3) p^ (1/2)",Dropping the minus sign (field opposite to p) or the far-field form for r >> a (2026 55/1/1 Q31(a)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5511-Q31A-a,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5511-Q31A-a; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-01-009,FAM-01-03 Electric dipole,01,T-01-08,DRV,Derive the torque on a dipole in a uniform field,Asks you to show that a dipole in a uniform field feels a turning effect pE sin(theta) but no net force.,Diagram; forces qE on both charges; net force zero; couple; torque = p x E,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-010,FAM-01-03 Electric dipole,01,T-01-08,PRD,Predict a dipole's motion in uniform and non-uniform fields,"Asks you to decide whether a dipole will turn, move, or both in a given field, and justify it.",Uniform: torque only; non-uniform: net force and torque; stable and unstable positions,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-011,FAM-01-04 Electric flux,01,T-01-09,NUM,Calculate electric flux through a surface or closed surface,"Asks you to find how much field passes through a surface, using E.A or Gauss's law for closed surfaces.",flux = EA cos(theta) or q/eps0; substitution; result with unit,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-012,FAM-01-05 Gauss's law applications,01,T-01-10,DEF,State Gauss's law and explain a Gaussian surface,Asks you to state Gauss's law in words and symbols and say how the imaginary closed surface is chosen.,Statement flux = q_enc/eps0; meaning of terms; choice of surface,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-013,FAM-01-05 Gauss's law applications,01,T-01-11,DRV,Derive the field of a long charged wire using Gauss's law,Asks you to use a cylindrical Gaussian surface to show that the field of a long charged wire falls off as one over the distance.,Cylinder diagram; flux through curved surface only; enclosed charge lambda*l; solve E = lambda/(2 pi eps0 r); direction radially outward for positive lambda,The direction of E is asked for and must be stated (2026 compartment 55/B/7 Q22(b)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026C-55B7-Q22B,"seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026C-55B7-Q22B; skeleton from the printed demand (no 55/7 scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-01-014,FAM-01-05 Gauss's law applications,01,T-01-12,DRV,Derive the field of an infinite charged sheet using Gauss's law,Asks you to use a small Gaussian cylinder through a large charged sheet to show that its field is normal to the sheet and the same at every distance.,"Gaussian cylinder through the sheet, E normal to it, figure (1/2); only the two flat faces contribute: net flux 2EA, charge enclosed sigma*A (1/2); 2EA = sigma*A/eps0 (1/2); vec(E) = (sigma/(2*eps0)) n^ (1/2)",No figure of the Gaussian cylinder loses its half mark (2026 55/1/1 Q22(a)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5511-Q22A-a,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5511-Q22A-a; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-01-015,FAM-01-05 Gauss's law applications,01,T-01-13,DRV,Derive the field inside and outside a charged thin shell,Asks you to use spherical Gaussian surfaces to show the field is zero inside and like a point charge outside.,Two spheres; symmetry; outside kQ/r^2; inside zero; E versus r graph,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-01-016,FAM-01-05 Gauss's law applications,01,T-01-12,NUM,Find the field between and outside two charged parallel sheets,"Asks you to add the fields of two large charged sheets, each the same at every distance, in the region between them and outside them.",each sheet gives sigma/(2*eps0) normal to it; between two like sheets the fields cancel: E = 0 (1/2); outside they add: E = sigma/eps0 (1/2),Adding the two fields between like-charged sheets (2026 55/1/1 Q22(b)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5511-Q22A-b-i,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5511-Q22A-b-i; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-02-001,FAM-02-01 Potential of charges and dipoles,02,T-02-04,NUM,Find the potential at a point due to several charges,"Asks you to add the potentials from each charge, as signed numbers, at a given point.","V at the point = sum of k*q_i/r_i over the charges, each with its sign; work to bring q_0 there = q_0 times that potential; result, zero where the potentials cancel","Dropping the signs of the charges, so that the potentials do not cancel (2026 compartment 55/7/3 Q23(ii))",VERIFIED,,seed,2026C-5573-Q23-ii,"seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026C-5573-Q23-ii; skeleton from the printed demand (no 55/7 scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-02-002,FAM-02-01 Potential of charges and dipoles,02,T-02-03,DRV,Derive the potential due to a dipole at a general point,"Asks you to show that a dipole's potential far away is kp cos(theta)/r^2, with axial and equatorial cases.",Diagram; potentials of +q and -q; approximation r >> a; result; special cases,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-02-003,FAM-02-01 Potential of charges and dipoles,02,T-02-02,GRF,Interpret potential and field versus distance graphs,Asks you to read or draw graphs of how potential and field change with distance from charges.,"V = k*Q/r, so the slope of V against 1/r is k*Q: a rising line means a positive charge, a falling line a negative one (1/2 + 1/2); Q_1/Q_2 = slope of A/slope of B (1); = tan(60 deg)/tan(30 deg), magnitude 3 (1)",Dropping the sign of the falling line's slope: the printed scheme gives 3/1 where Q_1/Q_2 = -3 (2026 55/3/1 Q31(a)(i)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5531-Q31A-i-I,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5531-Q31A-i-I; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-02-004,FAM-02-02 Equipotentials and field-potential relation,02,T-02-05,CON,Explain equipotential surfaces and why field is perpendicular to them,"Asks you to describe surfaces of equal potential, sketch them, and explain why field lines cross them at right angles.","a field not normal to the surface would have a component along it; moving a test charge against that component would need work, which contradicts the definition of an equipotential surface, so E is normal (1); alternatively Delta V = -vec(E).vec(Delta l) = 0 gives theta = 90 deg",Stating that the field is perpendicular without the work argument (2026 55/2/2 Q25(ii); 55/4/1 Q33(a)(i)(I)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5522-Q25-ii,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5522-Q25-ii; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-02-005,FAM-02-02 Equipotentials and field-potential relation,02,T-02-01,NUM,Find work done or field from a potential difference,"Asks you to use the potential difference to find the work to move a charge, or the field between points.",W = q dV; E = -dV/dr; substitution; result with unit and sign,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-02-006,FAM-02-03 Electrostatic potential energy,02,T-02-06,NUM,Find the potential energy of a system of charges,Asks you to add the energy of every pair of charges to find the work needed to build the arrangement.,"work = k*[q_1*q_2/r_12 + q_1*q_3/r_13 + q_2*q_3/r_23], one term per pair (1/2); substitution with the signs of the charges, = -k*10*q^2/a (1); work to dissociate = minus the potential energy, +k*10*q^2/a (1/2)",Leaving the sign: the work to dissociate is minus the potential energy of the system (2026 55/4/1 Q33(a)(ii)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5541-Q33A-ii,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5541-Q33A-ii; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-02-007,FAM-02-03 Electrostatic potential energy,02,T-02-07,DRV,Derive the potential energy of a dipole in a uniform field,Asks you to show a dipole's energy in a field is -pE cos(theta) and find the work to rotate it.,Work as integral of torque; integrate; reference angle; U = -p.E; work between angles,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-02-008,FAM-02-04 Conductors and dielectrics,02,T-02-08,CON,Explain electrostatics of conductors,"Asks you to explain why the field inside a conductor is zero, where its charge sits, and why the surface field is perpendicular.",Four properties with reasons; electrostatic shielding example,Saying the potential inside a conductor is zero instead of constant (SQP 2025-26 Q31(II)(C)),VERIFIED,,seed,SQP2526-042-Q31B-C,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines; promoted at Batch 0 by SQP2526-042-Q31B-C
PH-02-009,FAM-02-04 Conductors and dielectrics,02,T-02-09,CON,Explain polarisation of a dielectric and the reduced field,Asks you to describe how a dielectric's molecules respond to a field and why the field inside becomes weaker.,"polarisation of the molecules induces a field opposite to the external field, so the net field inside the dielectric is reduced (1); E = E_0 - E_p; a diagram earns full credit",Saying the dielectric blocks the field without naming the opposing induced field (2026 55/4/1 Q33(a)(i)(II)),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5541-Q33A-i-II,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5541-Q33A-i-II; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-02-010,FAM-02-05 Capacitors,02,T-02-12,DRV,Derive the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor with or without dielectric,Asks you to show C = eps0 A/d and how a dielectric slab or metal slab between the plates changes it.,"figure: plates of area A, separation d, charge densities sigma and -sigma; E = sigma/eps0 = q/(A*eps0) (1); V = E*d = q*d/(A*eps0) (1); C = q/V = A*eps0/d (1); with a slab V = E0(d-t) + E0 t/K",Using d instead of (d - t + t/K) or dropping K in the slab term (SQP 2025-26 Q31(I)(A)); leaving out the figure the first mark needs (2026 55/2/1 Q32(a)),VERIFIED,,seed,SQP2526-042-Q31A-A,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines; promoted at Batch 0 by SQP2526-042-Q31A-A; skeleton refined at Batch 2 from printed 2026 scheme lines (2026-5521-Q32A-a)
PH-02-011,FAM-02-05 Capacitors,02,T-02-11,NUM,Find equivalent capacitance and charges in a capacitor network,Asks you to combine capacitors in series and parallel and find the charge and voltage on each one.,"C_X = C, C_Y = K*C; 1/C_eq = 1/C_X + 1/C_Y (1/2); solve for C (1/2); C_X and C_Y (1/2); total charge Q = C_eq*V, the same on each capacitor in series (1/2); V_X = Q/C_X (1/2); V_Y = Q/C_Y, or V - V_X (1/2)","Adding series capacitances directly, or forgetting that capacitors in series carry equal charge (2026 55/5/1 Q22)",VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5551-Q22-a,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5551-Q22-a; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-02-012,FAM-02-05 Capacitors,02,T-02-13,NUM,Find the energy stored in a capacitor or combination,"Asks you to use the energy formula of a capacitor (formula only, no derivation) to find the stored energy.",Choose form of U; substitution; result with unit,,DRAFT,,seed,,recalled seed - DRAFT until a real instance verifies it; skeleton to be replaced by printed scheme lines
PH-02-013,FAM-02-05 Capacitors,02,T-02-12,PRD,Predict capacitor changes when a dielectric slab or the plate gap changes,"Asks you to decide how capacitance, charge, voltage, field and energy change when a slab goes in or out or the gap changes, and justify each.","identify what stays constant: Q with the battery disconnected, V with it connected; C = K*eps0*A/d, so C changes by the factor K (and d) (1/2); V = Q/C or Q = C*V, E = V/d (1/2); U = Q^2/(2C) or (1/2)*C*V^2 (1/2); state the increase or decrease with its factor (1/2)","Treating V as fixed after the battery is disconnected, or Q as fixed while it stays connected (2026 55/1/1 Q23; 55/2/1 Q32(b))",VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5511-Q23-a,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5511-Q23-a; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-02-014,FAM-02-05 Capacitors,02,T-02-11,NUM,Find the common potential and charges when capacitors are joined,"Asks you to use conservation of charge to find the shared voltage after a charged capacitor is joined to another, and the charge each one then holds.","initial charge Q_i = C_1*V_i (1/2); charge conserved, common potential V_f = C_1*V_i/(C_1 + C_2) (1/2 + 1/2); value (1/2); Q_1 = C_1*V_f (1/2); Q_2 = C_2*V_f (1/2)",Adding the voltages instead of sharing the charge (2026 55/1/2 Q26),VERIFIED,,seed,2026-5512-Q26,seed promoted at Batch 2 from 2026-5512-Q26; skeleton replaced by printed 2026 scheme lines

PH-01-031,FAM-01-03 Electric dipole,01,T-01-08,MCQ,Identify the direction of the torque on a dipole (MCQ),"Asks you to see that the torque on a dipole in a uniform field, p cross E, is perpendicular to both p and E.","1 mark for the option; vec(tau) = vec(p) x vec(E), a cross product, perpendicular to both vectors",Taking the torque along E or along p (2026 55/B Q29(iv)),VERIFIED,,2,2026-55B-Q29-iv,issued at Batch 2 from 2026-55B-Q29-iv; skeleton from printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-01-032,FAM-01-02 Electric field and field lines,01,T-01-05,DRV,Deduce the force on a charge from the field of another charge,Asks you to write the field of a point charge at a point and show that the force on a charge placed there is that charge times the field.,"field of Q at r: vec(E) = (1/(4*pi*eps0))*(Q/r^2) r^ (1/2); Coulomb force on q: vec(F) = (1/(4*pi*eps0))*(Q*q/r^2) r^, so vec(F) = q*vec(E) (1/2)","Writing magnitudes only, without the unit vector r^ (2026 55/B Q31(a)(i))",VERIFIED,,2,2026-55B-Q31A-a-i,issued at Batch 2 from 2026-55B-Q31A-a-i; skeleton from printed 2026 scheme lines
PH-01-033,FAM-01-05 Gauss's law applications,01,T-01-13,MCQ,Pick the field against distance graph of a charged conducting sphere (MCQ),Asks you to pick the graph showing zero field inside a charged conducting sphere and a field falling as one over distance squared outside it.,"1 mark for the option; E = 0 for x < R, E = kQ/R^2 at the surface, E = kQ/x^2 falling for x > R",Choosing a field that rises or stays constant inside the conductor (2026 compartment 55/7/1 Q2),VERIFIED,,2,2026C-5571-Q02,"issued at Batch 2 from 2026C-5571-Q02; skeleton from the printed demand (no 55/7 scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-01-034,FAM-01-05 Gauss's law applications,01,T-01-11,NUM,Find the net field at points near two parallel charged wires,"Asks you to find the field of each long charged wire at given points, with its direction, and add the two fields at each point.",E = lambda/(2*pi*eps0*r) for each wire; direction away from a positive and towards a negative line charge; vector sum at each point; result with unit and direction,"Subtracting the fields between oppositely charged wires, where they add (2026 compartment 55/7/1 Q28(a))",VERIFIED,,2,2026C-5571-Q28A,"issued at Batch 2 from 2026C-5571-Q28A; skeleton from the printed demand (no 55/7 scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-01-035,FAM-01-01 Coulomb's law and superposition,01,T-01-02,MCQ,Spot the wrong statement about the Coulomb force (MCQ),"Asks you to recall how the force between two charges depends on the charges, their distance and the medium, and pick the false statement.","1 mark for the option; F = q1*q2/(4*pi*eps0*eps_r*r^2): proportional to each charge, inverse square of distance, depends on the medium",Picking a true statement when the question asks for the one that is not correct (2026 compartment 55/B/7 Q2),VERIFIED,,2,2026C-55B7-Q02,"issued at Batch 2 from 2026C-55B7-Q02; skeleton from the printed demand (no 55/7 scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"

CS-2025-5541-Q30,2025-5541,30,"A passage on the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom: the electron (mass m, charge e) revolves round the proton in a circular orbit of radius r with speed v, the electrostatic attraction providing the centripetal force, and only orbits whose angular momentum is an integral multiple of h/(2*pi) are allowed. CS-2025-5551-Q30,2025-5551,30,"A passage on Einstein's explanation of the photoelectric effect from Planck's quantum theory: light travels as photons of energy h*nu, and the number of photons in a beam determines its intensity. # PHY-03 addendum (entries added at Batch 0; the full file was delivered as PHY-03-MISTAKES-LEDGER.md)

### G · Batch 0 (29 September)
- **B0-1 · The project's sample paper was last session's.** `Physics-SQP.pdf` prints "CLASS – XII (2025 – 26)"; CBSE reuses that file name every year, and PHY-04 §2's "SQP 2026-27" details (VI alternative inside Q9; text damage 168O, "B and B", 300) are absent from it. Caught at boot from the page-1 image.
  → A permanent file's session is read from its page-1 image, never from its name; a mismatch is logged and the file is mined for what it is → CI§7, P§5
- **B0-2 · Two "errors in the official syllabus" in PHY-04 §1 were text-layer damage.** The page-12 image prints 7 marks for Unit IX and "Chapter–14"; the text layer had moved the 7 into the chapter line.
  → A claimed error in an official document is recorded only after its page image confirms it → CI§2, P§6
- **B0-3 · The boot search pattern `pyqkit*.py*` misses the project copy `pyqkit_py.txt`.** The kit was found by listing the folder.
  → Boot also matches `pyqkit_py.txt`; the CI wording is queued for correction → CI§3
- **B0-4 · The first Batch 0 reply stopped at the tool limit before its checkpoint,** leaving the database copy older than the disk for one turn (nothing lost; `Resume` packed first).
  → Checkpoint right after the gate items, before opening a paper, as well as after each paper → CI§6
- **B0-5 · Inventory reads identity from text only;** the 2026 scheme bundles have near-empty text layers, so kind, year and paper id came out unknown.
  → Image-only files get their identity from their page images at S1 intake, through ERRATA → P§5

### Part 3 addition
- **W-13 · A permanent file replaced by last session's twin** (CBSE reuses names such as `Physics-SQP.pdf` every year).
  → Boot compares each permanent file's printed session with the one the CI names; a mismatch is logged in one line and never blocks → CI§7

### H · Batch 1 (29-30 September)
- **B1-1 · The first Batch 1 reply hit the tool limit before its first checkpoint (a repeat of B0-4).** About thirty separate calls went to boot reads and identity crops; the identity confirmations lived only in the chat until the next turn. Nothing was lost (the vault was unchanged), but a repeat is the worst outcome this ledger names.
  → Boot reads are batched into one or two calls; each stage's findings are written to disk by one script as soon as they are read; the first checkpoint comes right after S1, before any paper page is opened -> CI s6, P s11
- **B1-2 · A paper_id opened the wrong document.** After S1 gave each scheme its paper's paper_id, `render 2026-5511` rendered the scheme bundle; caught at once from the text printout, before any row was written.
  → Documents are opened by file_id; kit fix queued (Q-008) -> P s4
- **B1-3 · The kit could not total a case study whose choice sits inside one sub-part when sub-part marks are printed** (55/2/1 Q29, Q30): it summed each side alone, so the paper failed check-paper though nothing was wrong on the page.
  → Fixed once in kit edition 2026-09-30 (common sub-parts count with each alternative), tested on every mined paper plus a planted overflow, logged, shipped in tools/ -> CI s7, P s4
- **B1-4 · A test script rewrote a scratch table without closing the file before the check ran,** so the check read a half-written file and reported missing questions. Scratch copy only; the vault was never touched.
  → Test harnesses close (or use `with`) every file before calling the kit -> P s4
- **B1-5 · A row count was typed into a PROGRESS line by hand (79 for 55/3/1) instead of taken from the data; the kit had just printed 72.** Caught before the checkpoint went out; corrected from the table.
  → Progress lines take their counts from the tables in the same script, never from memory -> CI s2.7
- **B1-6 · The time estimate in a reply said 13 sibling papers were left; the tables said 12.** The count was typed before the tables were read.
  → Counts in replies, estimates included, come from a script run earlier in the same turn -> CI s2.7

### Part 3 additions (Batch 2, Claude Code route)
- **W-14 · Two miners writing one vault** (the chat and Claude Code at once): restore keeps only the newest copy, so the other one's work vanishes silently.
  → One writer at a time: Claude Code mines; the chat audits read only and sends `Fix:` lines → CLAUDE.md §3, PHY-07 R§13
- **W-15 · An agent that can run code is tempted to fill rows from the text layer with a script.**
  → Every value is read from a page image; the text layer only cross-checks digits; a blind second reading is compared by the gate before any merge → CI§2.2, PHY-07 R§6-R§8
- **W-16 · A long session compacts and loses rules held only in conversation.**
  → Rules live in CLAUDE.md (re-read after compaction); state lives on disk (PROGRESS, part files, pushed packs) → CLAUDE.md §9

### I · Batch 2 (1 October, first Claude Code session)
- **B2-1 · The setup gave the scheme repository no role.** The vault file sits in the instructions repository and the 2026 schemes in a repository with neither a vault file nor a ZIP, so `phy_code_env.py` linked none of the scheme PDFs and inventory would have missed every one. Caught at boot from the setup's role lines; the PDFs were linked into /mnt/project by hand (links only) before inventory ran as CLAUDE.md §6 writes it.
  → At boot, every repository found must have a role or be opened by hand before inventory; Q-011 → CLAUDE.md §6, R§2
- **B2-2 · R§3's `render <file_id>` stopped with "cannot find document"** because the kit's `--vault` defaults to empty. Nothing was written from it.
  → Pass `--vault /home/claude/vault` to `pages` and `render`; Q-011 → R§3
- **B2-3 · Batch 1 misread the polarity of one cell in 55/3/1 Q17(a)** (F-2026-5531-02 puts E_2's longer plates towards B; the page shows them towards C, so the cells oppose and EQ-2026-5531-003's E_1 + E_2 is wrong). Every number on the row was right, so neither check-paper nor a numbers-only double-read could see it; the B02 extractor found it by comparing the sibling figures on 600-dpi crops, and both B02 rows describe the page.
  → A figure whose meaning depends on polarity or direction (cells, diodes, arrows, field lines) gets a crop on which plate lengths or arrowheads are measured, and its FIGURES description names the orientation; the stored rows are corrected through ERRATA (Q-013) -> CI s2.2, P s6.4
- **B2-4 · The 55/B/7 extractor wrote note text into the options column of 36 non-MCQ rows** (2026C-55B7-Q19 to -Q33B-ii); the gate check passed it and only the blind double-read showed it.
  → options is filled only when q_type is MCQ or AR; the double-read stays on every paper → R§5, R§8

### J · Batch 3 (2 October; lessons from the Batch 2 audit)
- **B3-1 · Detail thinned at speed.** The overnight run (effort max) wrote figure descriptions of 143 characters against the trial's 201, 1.38 formula rows per numerical or derivation against 1.86, and notes on 35 % of new rows against 61 %; values were equally accurate, so no check saw it.
  → Every new row is written to the trial's level: complete stems, givens and unknown, every figure element with value, position and direction, given/asked/result formulas for the whole chain, a note on every new sibling row → PHY-08 Y§6
- **B3-2 · Note text passed through the options column** (2026C-55B7, 36 non-MCQ rows): the gate check of the time accepted it and only the blind double-read caught it.
  → Gate edition 2026-10-02 refuses `options` on a row whose q_type is not MCQ or AR → PHY-07 R§9, PHY-08 Y§7
- **B3-3 · A blank rel passed** (2026-5552, 15 new rows; fixed ER-B02-088..ER-B02-102).
  → Gate edition 2026-10-02 refuses a row with a blank `rel` → PHY-07 R§9, PHY-08 Y§7
- **B3-4 · The setup could not see a vault kept only on a branch**, so a new session would have found no vault on main.
  → Setup edition 2026-10-02b collects vault files from every branch, restores the newest and carries its branch forward → PHY-07 R§2, CLAUDE.md §3
- **B3-5 · Browser-renamed tool files broke the boot command** (`phy_gate (1).py`, `phy_code_env (2).py`, `PHY-07-CLAUDE-CODE-RUNBOOK (1).md`): the old command looked for exact names.
  → The boot command finds `phy_code_env*.py`; the setup links renamed copies under their plain names, picks the newest and names the extras → CLAUDE.md §6, PHY-07 R§2
- **B3-6 · Inventory files a sample paper's scheme as a board scheme** (Physics-MS.pdf 2025-26 at B02; the 2026-27 one again at B03: kind MS, exam MAIN, placeholder paper_id 2027-X7aec84).
  → Its identity is fixed at S1 from the page-1 image through ERRATA (kind SQP-MS, exam SQP, paper_id SQP<yy><yy>-042), as ER-B02-072..ER-B02-076 did → PHY-08 Y§0.4, P§5
- **B3-7 · Classification spent her usage on a stage she wanted later,** because the old CLAUDE.md said to go on until the year closed; she stopped it during chapter 03.
  → Printed documents of 2025 to 2022 first; S5-without-scheme, S6, S7 and S8 of every year are DEFERRED lines for the closing sweep and are never started without her → CLAUDE.md §12, PHY-08 Y§0
- **B3-8 · The year planner trusted code shape over FILES.** `--plan-year 2025` read the letter in 55/S/1 as a visually-impaired code and ignored sets_covered on the 2025 schemes, so PROGRESS lacked the compartment origin and called printed sibling schemes missing. Caught by reading the planned lines against FILES before the first paper.
  → After every `--plan-year`, check each planned line against FILES (series, exam, sets_covered) before mining; wrong lines are corrected through the gate and queued (Q-022), never by hand → CLAUDE.md §8, R§9

# Y2026 — Claude's observations (judged text; every point backed by instance ids)

## SQP 2025-26 (SQP2526-042) — mined at Batch 0, 2026-09-29
- **Prediction step (S6).** First paper in the vault: no archetype statistics existed, so nothing could be predicted. All 34 codes it needed beyond the seeds were issued new; 19 seed archetypes were promoted by it.
